transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm glad you're here today. What brings you to the clinic? What's been going on that made you decide to come in?

Hi. Um, thank you. Well, what brings me in is... I’ve just been waking up with this really heavy, hollow sadness lately. It’s hard to shake. I'm a choreographer, and the best way I can explain it is that it feels like the studio lights are on, but there’s just no music in me anymore. It's just a very flat, sad feeling, and I figured it was time to come in and talk to someone about it.
Have you experienced periods like this before in your life, where you felt this kind of persistent sadness and emptiness?

Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, I've had bad days or felt stressed out before, but... not like this. I haven't ever felt this kind of persistent emptiness. It's usually just a passing thing if I get down, so this feeling of it just dragging on and on is pretty new for me.
When did you first notice this feeling of sadness and emptiness starting? Can you pinpoint roughly when it began?
I'd say... it's been about nine months now. Yeah, if I look back, that's roughly when this depressed feeling really started and just sort of stayed.

During these past 9 months, has there been any time—even a week or two—where you felt back to your normal self, or has the sadness and emptiness been there pretty much every single day without breaks?

Um, no, there hasn't really been a break. It's... it's been pretty much every day. I haven't had a week or even a few days where I felt like my normal self again. It's just been a constant, heavy feeling the whole time.

Before these 9 months started, have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks where you felt depressed or lost interest in things you normally enjoy, even if it wasn't as severe as what you're experiencing now?

No, I don't think so. Like I was saying earlier, I'd have a bad day here or there, maybe get a little burnt out from choreographing or teaching, but... it never lasted for two whole weeks. Before this nine-month stretch started, I always bounced back pretty quickly. So, no, nothing like that.

Before these 9 months started, looking back over your whole life, was there ever a time—maybe a few months or longer—when you felt a bit down, less interested in things, or just not quite yourself, even if it was much milder than what you're experiencing now?

Um, no, honestly I can't think of a time like that. Before these last nine months, I was always really active and engaged with my dancing and my life. I never really went through a phase where I felt down or disconnected for months at a time, even mildly. This whole experience is pretty much a first for me.

Around the time these 9 months ago when this sadness started, did anything significant happen in your life—like a loss, a major change, a relationship issue, or something stressful—that you think might have triggered this feeling?

No, not really. I mean, I've thought about that a lot, trying to figure out why this happened. But... there wasn't any big event. No breakups, no one died, my career was going fine. It just sort of... started. I don't really have a reason for it.

Have you ever had a period—maybe a few days or longer—where you felt unusually energetic, euphoric, or 'up,' needed much less sleep than usual, or felt like you could do anything? I'm asking about times when your mood or energy was elevated, not depressed.

Yes, actually. There were stretches in the past where I felt... I guess just dazzlingly alive. Really energetic and up. But it wasn't always just a good feeling. During those same times, I would get suddenly furious if anyone questioned my plans or... well, if they reminded me that my ankle still needed rest, I would just snap. So yeah, I've definitely had periods like that.
When you had those periods where you felt dazzlingly alive and energetic, how long did those stretches typically last? Were we talking about a few days, a week or two, or longer?

Well, this whole pattern with the high energy and then getting angry... it actually started after I injured my ankle. So, it's been going on for about two months now. It's just been this consistent stretch for the last couple of months.

During those two months when you felt dazzlingly alive and energetic, did you notice that you needed significantly less sleep than usual—like feeling rested after only a few hours—or did you experience racing thoughts or a flood of ideas?

Yeah, my sleep has been all over the place, honestly. Like, some nights I would just stay up sketching dance formations until dawn, and I felt completely fine doing it. But lately... well, I'll fall asleep just exhausted, but then I wake up at four or five in the morning and my stomach is just tight. So I definitely haven't been sleeping normally.

When you were staying up sketching dance formations until dawn, did you feel like you needed less sleep than usual—like you felt genuinely rested and energized on just a few hours—or were you staying up because your mind was racing with ideas and you couldn't fall asleep?

I guess... I'm not really sure, to be honest. I didn't really think about it like that at the time. I just... I was up and I was working. I don't know if I felt genuinely rested on just a few hours, or if I just couldn't sleep because I had so many ideas going on. It's hard to tell the difference looking back. I just know I was awake and I didn't feel exhausted while I was doing it.

During those two months when you were staying up late sketching and feeling energetic, on the nights you slept just a few hours, did you actually feel well-rested and recharged the next day, or did you feel tired but your mind was just too active to let you sleep?

I don't really know how to answer that. I just... I haven't really paid attention to whether I felt recharged or just too wired to sleep. I just know I was awake and I didn't feel tired during the day. I was just going about my day, working on my routines, and I felt fine. I didn't feel like I was dragging or anything. But I can't really say if it was because I was rested or just running on adrenaline.

Before you injured your ankle two months ago, during the nine months before that when you were feeling depressed, were there any times when you felt noticeably more energetic, more talkative, or in a better mood than you do right now—times when you felt more like your normal self or even better than your normal self?

No, not really. Before I hurt my ankle, those whole nine months... I was just down. I didn't have any days where I felt energetic or talkative, or even just like my normal self. It was just a long stretch of feeling really low and exhausted. There weren't any breaks in it where I felt good or upbeat.

When you were feeling that dazzling energy and staying up sketching for those two months after your ankle injury, did you feel like you were in an unusually great mood or happy—like your mood was elevated or euphoric—or was it more that you felt driven to work and irritable if interrupted, but not necessarily happy?

I think it was a bit of both, honestly. There were stretches when I felt just... dazzlingly alive, like everything was perfect and I was in a great mood. But then I would get suddenly furious if anyone questioned the plan I was working on, or... or if they reminded me that my ankle still needed rest. So I felt really happy and driven, but I had a very short fuse if someone tried to slow me down or get in my way.
